userStories.title: Add get_sm_holdings() to scanner.py — SM wallet count and token holdings from Nansen
userStories.description:
Current state: scanner.py at businesses/horizen-zkverify/base-trader/scripts/scanner.py has get_sm_netflow() which returns zeros for net_flow_1h, net_flow_7d, net_flow_30d, and trader_count because it only reads from the screener cache (which only has 24h netflow).

Nansen has an endpoint POST /api/v1/smart-money/holdings that returns tokens SM wallets hold on a given chain, including wallet counts and holding amounts. This is 10 credits per call.

What to build:
1. Add a new disk-cached function get_sm_holdings(chain='base') with 4-hour TTL (same pattern as holders cache):
   - Cache file: DATA_DIR / 'sm_holdings_cache.json'
   - On cache miss: POST to https://api.nansen.ai/api/v1/smart-money/holdings with body {"chain": "base"}
   - Parse response: extract token_address, sm_wallet_count, total_value_usd, token_symbol
   - Return dict keyed by token_address.lower() -> {sm_wallet_count, total_value_usd, symbol}
   - Log credits used: 10 per call

2. Update get_sm_netflow() to enrich its return value with SM holdings data:
   - Call get_sm_holdings() (from cache, no extra API call)
   - Look up the token in the holdings dict
   - Set trader_count = sm_wallet_count from holdings (instead of 0)
   - This makes the SM pillar in signal_filter.py actually score above 20

Constraints:
- Do NOT modify signal_filter.py, run_pipeline.py, or any other file
- Keep existing screener-based 24h netflow logic — holdings data supplements, doesn't replace
- Mock mode must return realistic mock data (trader_count > 0)
- Cache must follow the existing _holders_cache pattern exactly (TTL check, disk read/write, freshness check)
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -c "import sys,os; os.environ['NANSEN_MOCK']='1'; sys.path.insert(0,'businesses/horizen-zkverify/base-trader/scripts'); from scanner import get_sm_netflow; r=get_sm_netflow('0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631'); assert r['trader_count'] > 0, f'trader_count still 0: {r}'; print(f'trader_count={r["trader_count"]} PASS')"
userStories.notes:
Implemented get_sm_holdings() function in scanner.py with 4-hour disk cache (sm_holdings_cache.json). The function:
1. Caches SM holdings data from Nansen's POST /api/v1/smart-money/holdings endpoint

userStories.title: Add get_flow_intelligence() to scanner.py — multi-timeframe buy/sell pressure from Nansen
userStories.description:
Current state: scanner.py returns zeros for net_flow_1h, net_flow_7d, net_flow_30d in get_sm_netflow(). Nansen has POST /api/v1/tgm/flow-intelligence which returns multi-timeframe buy/sell pressure for a specific token (10 credits per call).

What to build:
1. Add get_flow_intelligence(token_address, chain='base') with per-token disk cache (4h TTL):
   - Cache file: DATA_DIR / 'flow_intelligence_cache.json' (keyed by address)
   - On cache miss: POST to https://api.nansen.ai/api/v1/tgm/flow-intelligence with body {"token_address": token_address, "chain": chain}
   - Parse response to extract multi-timeframe net flow data
   - Return dict with: net_flow_1h_usd, net_flow_24h_usd, net_flow_7d_usd, net_flow_30d_usd, buy_pressure_pct, sell_pressure_pct
   - 10 credits per cache miss

2. Update get_sm_netflow() to use flow intelligence data when available:
   - After getting screener netflow (24h), call get_flow_intelligence()
   - If flow intelligence returns data, use its multi-timeframe values instead of zeros
   - If flow intelligence fails (API error, no data), fall back to existing zeros
   - This activates the multi-timeframe scoring in signal_filter.py

Constraints:
- Do NOT call get_flow_intelligence() for every token — only call it when scanner.py is invoked with enrichment (add an enrich=True parameter to get_sm_netflow)
- run_pipeline.py will need to pass enrich=True for tokens that pass initial screening (but do NOT modify run_pipeline.py in this story)
- Mock mode must return realistic multi-timeframe data
- Cache per token with 4h TTL (not a bulk cache like screener)
acceptanceCriteria: python3 -c "import sys,os; os.environ['NANSEN_MOCK']='1'; sys.path.insert(0,'businesses/horizen-zkverify/base-trader/scripts'); from scanner import get_sm_netflow; r=get_sm_netflow('0x940181a94a35a4569e4529a3cdfb74e38fd98631', enrich=True); assert r['net_flow_7d_usd'] != 0, f'7d still 0: {r}'; print(f'7d={r["net_flow_7d_usd"]} PASS')"

userStories.title: Wire enriched SM data into run_pipeline.py — two-tier evaluation
userStories.description:
Current state: run_pipeline.py at businesses/horizen-zkverify/base-trader/scripts/run_pipeline.py calls get_sm_netflow(address) without enrichment for every token. This means flow intelligence (multi-timeframe data) is never fetched.

What to build:
1. Implement two-tier evaluation in the token processing loop:

   Tier 1 (cheap): For every token, compute a preliminary score using:
   - Price structure pillar (from S/R)
   - Token health pillar (from pool TVL + holders)
   - SM pillar with screener-only data (existing behavior)
   If preliminary score < 100, skip to next token.

   Tier 2 (enriched): For tokens that pass Tier 1 (score >= 100):
   - Call get_sm_netflow(address, enrich=True) to get multi-timeframe flow data
   - Re-score with the enriched data
   - This is where the full 4-pillar scoring actually works
   - Cap enriched evaluations at 5 per run (credit budget)

2. Add a counter: enriched_count. After 5 enriched evaluations, remaining tokens use Tier 1 only.

3. Log tier in signal_log.jsonl: add 'tier': 1 or 'tier': 2 to the record.

Constraints:
- Keep the existing pipeline flow intact — tier evaluation is additive
- Do NOT modify scanner.py, signal_filter.py, or any other script
- The 5-per-run cap must be configurable via settings.json (key: max_enriched_per_run, default: 5)
- Credit impact: ~50-60 credits per run when 5 tokens are enriched (holdings cache + 5 × flow_intelligence)
